title: 1905 Salad
description:
This is the famous “1905” Salad from the Columbia Restaurant in Ybor City, in Tampa. This family
favorite was founded in 1905.
As kids, we had this on those special occasions that we went out to eat, either at the Columbia or Las Novidadas, both excellent Spanish restaurants in the Latin/Cuban quarter of downtown Tampa.
It was here that I got to practice my Spanish and learned that the proper way to pronounce “iced tea” was not “ei-ka tee-ah” as I stupidly tried on my first visit (much to my parents' shock!).
It was here also that, as kids, we had our first taste of Paella, though we never protested with “Pie Eh Ugh!” signs, as did our oh-so- rebellious daughters.
“1905” Salad
ingredients: ½ cup Swiss cheese, cut in
½ cup tasty ham, cut in julienne
Toss together all the salad ingredients. (I was out of celery this day, so I used radishes.)
directions: Drop the peeled garlic cloves one at a time into a running food process to mince.
Add the rest of the dressing ingredients (except the olive oil) to the food processor bowl.
With the motor running, slowly add the olive oil to form an emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add the dressing to the salad and toss well.
Here we made it another day, with some of the ingredients on the side (so Mommy can leave out the meat and onions!).
